section.name: Overview
section.p: Extracting data from web pages is one of the primary use cases for HtmlUnit. Because HtmlUnit models a real web browser (including DOM tree generation, CSS evaluation, and JavaScript execution), it offers powerful capabilities for extracting structured data, raw text, HTML fragments, and element attributes.

section.name: Extracting Rendered Text with asNormalizedText()
section.p: The primary method for extracting human-readable content from any DOM node or page is asNormalizedText().
Unlike standard raw text getters, asNormalizedText() simulates how text is actually rendered on screen:

ul.li: Collapses consecutive whitespace sequences into single spaces.

Appends line breaks (\n) between block-level CSS elements (such as

,

, or ).
Ignores invisible DOM elements like <script> and <style> tags.
Respects CSS visibility settings, excluding content hidden via rules such as display: none or visibility: hidden.

subsection.name: Extracting Text from the Entire Page
subsection.p: Calling asNormalizedText() directly on the HtmlPage or HtmlBody retrieves all visible text across the document.

section.name: Extracting HTML / XML Source
section.p: If you need the underlying markup rather than plain text, HtmlUnit provides asXml() on all DOM nodes.

subsection.name: Serializing the DOM with asXml()
subsection.p: Calling asXml() serializes the current state of a node (and its child subtree) into valid XML/HTML markup. Because it reads from the active DOM tree, it includes any dynamic changes made by JavaScript after page load.

ul.li: Calling page.asXml() returns the entire rendered document markup.
Calling element.asXml() returns the HTML/XML representation of that specific element and its descendants.

section.name: Extracting Attributes and Links
section.p: When scraping web sites, extracting element attributes (such as href, src, or data-* attributes) is common.

subsection.name: Navigating Links: Prefer .click() over Extracting href
subsection.p: With traditional raw scrapers, navigating to a new page typically requires extracting the href attribute string and manually issuing a new GET request.
Because HtmlUnit simulates a real browser, in most cases you do not need to extract the href attribute. Instead, simply call click() directly on the anchor element:
Using click() is strongly recommended over extracting `href` manually because it:

ul.li: Triggers any attached JavaScript onclick event handlers.
Handles single-page application (SPA) client-side routing.
Resolves relative paths, base tags, and redirects automatically.
Maintains browser session state, cookies, and window history.

section.name: Extracting Lists (<ol> and <ul>)
section.p: When calling asNormalizedText() on list elements, HtmlUnit automatically formats the text to mirror how browsers visually present list contents.

subsection.name: Ordered Lists (<ol>)
subsection.p: For ordered lists, asNormalizedText() automatically inserts sequential numbers (e.g., 1. , 2. ) before each list item (<li>) and places each item on its own line. HtmlUnit also respects the start attribute on <ol> tags, starting the sequence from the specified initial number. Any direct text nodes inside the list that are not wrapped in an <li> tag are preserved on separate lines without numbers.

subsection.name: Unordered Lists (<ul>)
subsection.p: For unordered lists, asNormalizedText() outputs each item on its own line without bullet symbols or numerical prefixes.

section.name: Extracting Data from Form Controls
section.p: Interactive form elements like text boxes, drop-down select lists, radio buttons, and checkboxes store their primary data in specific DOM properties rather than plain text nodes. HtmlUnit provides specialized node types to easily query their current values and states.

In addition to inspecting property values directly, asNormalizedText() also handles form controls seamlessly—returning the visible text or user-entered value (such as selected drop-down options or input box text) exactly as rendered by the browser.

subsection.name: Text Input Controls (<input type='text'>)
subsection.p: When calling asNormalizedText() on a text input element (or an enclosing parent like <body> or <form>), HtmlUnit extracts the currently displayed user value—including any text typed dynamically or modified by user interactions—rather than the initial static HTML attribute string.
Calling asNormalizedText() reflects the active state of the input field as a user sees it in the browser window:
subsection.h4: 2. Direct Value Extraction: getValue() vs. getValueAttribute()
subsection.p: When reading input values programmatically, it is important to distinguish between the current dynamic state and the original HTML markup:

ul.li: getValue(): Returns the current dynamic value of the input (equivalent to what asNormalizedText() retrieves and what JavaScript reads via element.value).
getValueAttribute(): Returns the original HTML attribute value as defined in the markup (e.g., <input value="...">), which remains unchanged when a user types into the field.

subsection.name: Text Area Controls (<textarea>)
subsection.p: For multiline text areas (<textarea>), asNormalizedText() returns the raw text content preserved across lines, including line breaks, while treating any child HTML tags inside the textarea strictly as literal text rather than rendered markup.

Calling asNormalizedText() on an HtmlTextArea (or an enclosing parent element like <body>) extracts the current multiline text as displayed in the control. Like text inputs, if a user updates or types new text into the area, asNormalizedText() dynamically reflects the updated content.
To retrieve the current text value programmatically from an HtmlTextArea instance, use getText():

subsection.name: Buttons (<input type='submit|reset'> and <button>)
subsection.p: When extracting text from button controls, asNormalizedText() returns the label visible to the user in the browser window, taking default browser labels and whitespace normalization into account.
subsection.h4: 1. Form Action Inputs (<input type="submit"> and <input type="reset">)
subsection.p: For input buttons, asNormalizedText() resolves the visible label based on the value attribute:

ul.li: Default Labels: If no value attribute is provided (e.g., <input type="submit">), asNormalizedText() returns the fixed default label ("Submit Query" for submit buttons or "Reset" for reset buttons), even though the value attribute itself remains empty. Note that HtmlUnit's default labels are static constants and are never localized.
Custom Labels: If a custom value is declared (e.g., value="Submit Request"), asNormalizedText() returns that custom label.
Explicitly Empty Labels: If value="" is set, asNormalizedText() returns an empty string.

subsection.p: For standard <button> elements, asNormalizedText() extracts the inner text content, automatically collapsing extra spaces, tabs, and newlines into single spaces just as a web browser renders them.

subsection.name: Radio Buttons & Checkboxes (<input type='radio|checkbox'>)
subsection.p: For toggle controls like radio buttons and checkboxes, asNormalizedText() explicitly prepends the control's current state ("checked" or "unchecked") to represent its visual checked status in plain text.

Calling asNormalizedText() directly on an HtmlRadioButtonInput or HtmlCheckBoxInput returns either "checked" or "unchecked". When called on a parent container (such as <form> or <body>), the checked state text is automatically combined with adjacent labels.
To check the state of radio buttons and checkboxes programmatically in code, use the boolean isChecked() method:

subsection.name: Select Elements (<select>) & Drop-Down Lists
subsection.p: For drop-down and list controls (<select>), asNormalizedText() returns the text of the currently selected option(s), formatted on separate lines.
The output of asNormalizedText() directly mirrors what is visually selected by the user in the control:

ul.li: Single / Default Select: For standard drop-downs (or multi-selects with active selections), asNormalizedText() returns the visible labels of all selected <option> elements separated by newline characters (\n).
Empty or Unselected Selects: If a <select> contains no options (or no selected option), asNormalizedText() returns an empty string.

subsection.p: When you need to inspect options programmatically (including non-selected items or option values vs. labels), use getSelectedOptions() or getOptions():

section.name: Tables, Formatting, and Advanced Element Handling
section.p: In addition to standard block and inline elements, asNormalizedText() applies specialized formatting rules to complex DOM structures such as tables, preformatted text, inline frames, and structural tags.

subsection.name: Extracting Tables (<table>, <tr>, <td>)
subsection.p: When serializing tables, asNormalizedText() formats rows and cells to preserve structural alignment in plain text:

ul.li: Cell Delimiters: Cells (<td>, <th>) within the same row are separated by a tab character (\t).
Row Separation: Each table row (<tr>) is placed on a new line.

Section Ordering: Table headers (<thead>) are serialized first, body rows (<tbody>) second, and footers (<tfoot>) last, ensuring consistent logical output regardless of element order in the underlying HTML markup.
Captions: Table captions (<caption>) are extracted at the top of the table on their own block line.

subsection.p: For deeper table manipulation details, see the dedicated Tables guide.

subsection.name: Preformatted Text (<pre>)
subsection.p: Unlike standard HTML elements where consecutive spaces, tabs, and newlines are collapsed into single spaces, asNormalizedText() preserves all whitespace, tabs, and newlines inside <pre> tags.

subsection.name: Inline Frames (<iframe>)
subsection.p: If an <iframe> is visible, asNormalizedText() recursively serializes the entire text content of the enclosed frame's document inline within the parent page text.

subsection.name: Ignored Tags & Special Handling
subsection.p: Certain HTML elements are treated specially during text normalization:

ul.li: Ignored Elements: <script>, <style>, <noframes> tags, and HTML comments are completely excluded from text extraction.
<noscript> Tags: If JavaScript is enabled in the WebClient (default), <noscript> contents are ignored. If JavaScript is disabled, their contents are included as standard text.
Non-Breaking Spaces ( ): Non-breaking space characters (  / \u00A0) are automatically converted into regular space characters (' ').
Document Title (<title>): Calling asNormalizedText() directly on an HtmlTitle element extracts the title string without evaluating external CSS stylesheets, optimizing performance.

section.name: Combining HtmlUnit with Jsoup
section.p: If you prefer Jsoup's fluent CSS selector and DOM manipulation API for content extraction, you can use the official htmlunit-jsoup bridge. This allows HtmlUnit to handle JavaScript execution and browser navigation, while providing a Jsoup Document interface for extraction.
